'''Ryan Kenwood Hollins'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.californiabirthindex.org/birth/ryan_kenwood_hollins_born_1984_16355629|title=Ryan Kenwood Hollins was born on October 10, 1984 in Los Angeles County, California|website=californiabirthindex.org|publisher=[[California Birth Index]]|access-date=May 28, 2020}}</ref> (born October 10, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is a color commentator for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rockets Announce Broadcast Teams|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-announce-broadcast-teams|access-date=2021-10-01|website=Houston Rockets|language=en}}</ref> He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He was a {{convert|7|ft|m|adj=on}} [[center (basketball)|center]] who was a [[Journeyman (sports)|journeyman]] in the NBA, playing for nine teams in 10 seasons.<ref>{{cite news|last=Buha|first=Jovan|title=The Grizzlies have a PG-13 nickname for journeyman Ryan Hollins|date=March 29, 2016|website=FoxSports.com|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/memphis-grizzlies-booty-call-tony-allen-ryan-hollins-nickname-032916|access-date=January 6, 2019}}</ref> He played briefly in Europe before ending his career.

Following his playing career, he pursued work in broadcasting, working as a game analyst for [[CBS]] and as a studio analyst for [[Los Angeles Clippers]] games. He also worked as an analyst for [[ESPN]] and appeared on various programming for them, including [[SportsCenter]] and [[First Take (talk show)|First Take]], and has co-hosted "The Opinionated 7-Footers" podcast for the past year. He joined the Houston Rockets' broadcasting team on [[AT&T SportsNet Southwest|AT&T SportsNet]] as a color commentator.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rockets Announce Broadcast Teams|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-announce-broadcast-teams|access-date=2021-10-01|website=Houston Rockets|language=en}}</ref>

==High school and college career==
Hollins attended [[John Muir High School (Pasadena, California)|John Muir High School]] in [[Pasadena, California]]. He had signed with [[Saint Louis University (United States)|St. Louis University]], but was allowed to withdraw his [[letter of intent]] after St. Louis head coach [[Lorenzo Romar]] left to become the head coach at the [[University of Washington]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-may-22-sp-prepbriefs22.2-story.html|title=Hollins Won't Attend Saint Louis|date=May 22, 2002|work=LATiimes.com|access-date=December 5, 2015}}</ref> After declining St. Louis, Hollins committed to and enrolled at UCLA.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tracy|last=Pierson|url=http://www.scout.com/college/ucla/story/50457-hollins-commits-to-ucla|title=Hollins Commits to UCLA|date=June 10, 2002|work=Scout.com|access-date=December 5, 2015}}</ref>

Hollins played significant minutes all four years of his career at [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. He had career averages of 5.5 points and 4 rebounds. He had a then career-high 11 points, 11 rebounds and seven blocks in a career-high 34 minutes<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hollins_ryan00.html |title=Ryan Hollins UCLA Player Profile |work=UCLABruins.cstv.com |access-date=October 4, 2015 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090101112808/http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hollins_ryan00.html |archive-date=January 1, 2009 }}</ref> against Oregon on January 30, 2003,<ref>{{cite news|title=Bruins mired in longest skid since 1945-46 season|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=230300026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030211033831/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=230300026|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 11, 2003|access-date=January 31, 2003|work=ESPN.com|date=January 31, 2003}}</ref> and bettered his career high with 21 points in a loss to USC on January 28, 2004.<ref>{{cite news|title=USC 76, UCLA 69|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=240280026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040227110144/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=240280026|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 27, 2004|access-date=January 28, 2004|work=ESPN.com|date=January 28, 2004}}</ref> He was named the Oakland Regional's Most Outstanding Player after registering 14 points and 9 rebounds in a 50–45 victory against the Memphis Tigers.<ref>{{cite news|title=Afflalo, UCLA clamp down on Memphis, stamp Final Four ticket|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060427215854/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000015|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 27, 2006|access-date=March 25, 2006|work=ESPN.com|date=March 25, 2006}}</ref>

Hollins was also an accomplished high jumper, clearing 6'10" at the [[Pac-10]] championships. In 2003, Hollins placed ninth in the high jump at the NCAA Regionals and sixth at the Pac-10 Championships.

==Professional career==
[[File:Ryan Hollins.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Hollins with Cleveland dunking against [[Yi Jianlian]] of the [[Washington Wizards]].]]

=== NBA (2006–2016) ===
Hollins was drafted in the second round (50th pick overall) of the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]]. He was the 100th UCLA player to be selected in the NBA draft. He played in 27 games and averaged 2.6 points per game during his rookie season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CHA/2007.html|title=2006-07 Charlotte Bobcats Roster and Stats|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=February 22, 2023}}</ref>

During 2008 off season, Bobcats extended him a qualifying offer and he became a [[restricted free agent]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/offers_extended_080701.html|title=Offers Extended to Okafor and Hollins, Option Picked Up on Davidson|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2008|access-date=August 4, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116031230/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/offers_extended_080701.html|archive-date=January 16, 2009}}</ref> On July 25, 2008, he signed this qualifying offer to stay one more year with the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/sign_hollins_080725.html|title=Bobcats Re-sign Ryan Hollins|work=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2008|access-date=August 4, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080915155738/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/sign_hollins_080725.html|archive-date=September 15, 2008}}</ref>

On January 16, 2009, Hollins was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] along with [[Matt Carroll (basketball)|Matt Carroll]] in exchange for [[DeSagana Diop]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/Mavericks_Acquisitions.html|title=Mavericks Acquire Carroll and Hollis; Trade Diop|work=NBA.com|date=January 16, 2009|access-date=January 17, 2009}}</ref>

On August 3, 2009, he was signed by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] to a three-year, $7 million offer sheet.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Wolves_Sign_Ryan_Hollins-090803.html|title=Wolves Sign Restricted Free Agent Ryan Hollins|work=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2009|access-date=August 4, 2009}}</ref> The Mavericks did not match the offer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/stories/080409dnspomavslede.39841c9.html|title=Dallas Mavericks won't match T-wolves' offer to Hollins|work=Dallas Morning News|author=Nichols, Bill|date=August 10, 2009|access-date=August 10, 2009|archive-date=August 7, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090807221820/http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/stories/080409dnspomavslede.39841c9.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 26, 2010, Hollins was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] along with guard [[Ramon Sessions]] and a second round pick in [[2013 NBA Draft|2013]] in exchange for [[Delonte West]] and [[Sebastian Telfair]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/trade_100726.html|title=Cavaliers Acquire Sessions and Hollins from Minnesota|work=NBA.com|date =July 26, 2010|access-date=July 27, 2010}}</ref>

He was released by the Cavaliers on March 20, 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Unable to maintain playing time, Ryan Hollins waived on Tuesday: Cavaliers Insider|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2012/03/cleveland_cavaliers_waive_cent.html|access-date=March 20, 2012|work=Cleveland.com|date=March 20, 2012}}</ref> He was then signed by the [[Boston Celtics]] on March 23, 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Celtics sign center Ryan Hollins|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7727486/boston-celtics-sign-center-ryan-hollins-waive-chris-wilcox|access-date=March 24, 2012|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2012}}</ref> Signed primarily to add size to the Celtic bench, Hollins played sparingly through 15 regular season games. Hollins played in 17 of the 20 postseason games, providing quality energy and rebounding at times when rookie [[Greg Stiemsma]] was in foul trouble.<ref>{{cite news|title=Report Card: Ryan Hollins|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4695306/report-card-ryan-hollins|work=ESPN.com|date=June 18, 2012|access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref>

On July 23, 2012, Hollins signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-ryan-hollins | title = CLIPPERS SIGN RYAN HOLLINS | work = NBA.com | date = July 23, 2012 | access-date = July 23, 2012}}</ref> On July 10, 2013, he re-signed with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-matt-barnes-darren-collison-ryan-hollins-and-chris-paul | title = CLIPPERS SIGN MATT BARNES, DARREN COLLISON, RYAN HOLLINS AND CHRIS PAUL | work = NBA.com | date = July 10, 2013 | access-date = July 10, 2013}}</ref>

On September 18, 2014, Hollins signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Kings Sign Center Ryan Hollins|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-center-ryan-hollins|access-date=September 18, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 18, 2014}}</ref>

=== Herbalife Gran Canaria (2016–2017) ===
On December 5, 2016, Hollins signed with [[CB Gran Canaria|Herbalife Gran Canaria]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 ACB season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cbgrancanaria.net/noticias/english-news/ryan-hollins-signs-for-herbalife-gran-canaria/|title=Ryan Hollins signs for Herbalife Gran Canaria|work=cbgrancanaria.net|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref>

On March 15, 2017, he was released from Gran Canaria due to disciplinary reasons, for having traveled to the United States, without permission and with the negative expression of the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cbgrancanaria.net/noticias/liga-endesa/comunicado-oficial-del-c-b-gran-canaria-3/|title=Comunicado oficial del C.B. Gran Canaria|work=cbgrancanaria.net|language=es|date=March 15, 2016|access-date=March 16, 2016}}</ref>

=== Auxilium Torino (2017) ===
Three days after being released from Herbalife Gran Canaria, Hollins signed with the Italian club [[Auxilium Pallacanestro Torino|Auxilium Torino]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 Lega Basket Serie A|2016–17 LBA season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fiat Torino inks Ryan Hollins|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/229320/fiat-torino-inks-ryan-hollins.html|access-date=March 18, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=March 18, 2017}}</ref>

=== Killer 3's (2018) ===
In April 2018, Ryan Hollins was selected by [[Killer 3's]] with the ninth overall pick of the [[2018 Big3 season|2018 BIG3]] draft.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-13 |title=BIG3 Season 2 Draft Review |url=https://big3.com/news/big3-season-2-draft-review/ |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Aliens (2019) ===
In 2019, Hollins spent the [[2019 Big3 season|BIG3 season]] playing for the [[Aliens (basketball)|Aliens]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ryan Hollins |url=https://big3.com/players/ryan-hollins/ |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 3's Company (2021) ===
In July 2021, Hollins joined [[3's Company]] led by coach [[Michael Cooper]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-08 |title=Ryan Hollins says he works like, "PB&J" with Mario Chalmers in the pick-and-roll. |url=https://big3.com/news/ryan-hollins-says-he-works-like-pbj-with-mario-chalmers-in-the-pick-and-roll/ |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Triplets (2022–present) ===
On May 25, 2022, Hollins was drafted by the [[Triplets (basketball)|Triplets]] with the sixth pick in the first round of the 2022 [[Big3]] draft.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-26 |title=2022 BIG3 Draft Recap |url=https://big3.com/news/2022-big3-draft-recap/ |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==National team career==

==Personal life==
Hollins is the son of Teryl and the late Denier Hollins.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA player Ryan Hollins to represent Jamaica|url=http://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/nba-player-ryan-hollins-to-represent-jamaica|access-date=June 7, 2013|work=Sportskeeda.com|date=June 7, 2013}}</ref>
